title: rmux — A terminal workspace built for responsiveness
excerpt: A native terminal workspace built for responsiveness. Rust, GPU rendering and Ghostty, with split panes and project workspaces.
content_html:
A native terminal. Written in Rust.

This isn’t
a screenshot.

It’s rmux, running in your browser.

Split a pane. Switch projects. Type help. Get a feel for it before you install.

Try the workspace below

rmux / live demoWASM · sample sessions

Shared rmux UI code. The same Ghostty terminal engine.
Sample sessions only; no shell or server connection.

Open full-size demo

On your desktop

A place for the
rest of your work.

Your editor is only part of a project. rmux keeps the shell, dev server and coding agent together in a workspace of tabs and split panes.

Move around with the keyboard, find commands in the palette, and return to a saved layout. Working in VS Code? Open the current project’s terminal workspace with its usual external-terminal shortcut.

Set up the VS Code workflow

Built to stay responsive

Rust. GPU rendering. Ghostty.

Input latency, idle CPU and memory use matter in a terminal you leave open all day. Those are development priorities, including when you have several panes running.

Read the measurements and remaining work

Take it out of the browser

Get rmux.

v0.1.15

macOS is signed and notarized, with Sparkle updates. Windows is unsigned. Linux requires Ubuntu 24.04 or compatible libraries.
